title: Zoo Platform
intro: This is how a request travels through the service. Drag each pattern block onto the place where it belongs, then link it to the components it talks to. A block is right when it sits in the right place and talks to exactly the right components.

blocks.label: Answer cache
blocks.blurb: Remembers deterministic answers for every replica.

blocks.label: Rate limiter
blocks.blurb: Two budgets per caller, shared by every replica.

blocks.label: Resilient model client
blocks.blurb: Deadlines, retries with jitter, circuit breakers, backup model.

blocks.label: Idempotency store
blocks.blurb: Remembers request keys and their responses.

blocks.label: Telemetry
blocks.blurb: Request ids, JSON logs, metrics and burn-rate alerts.

blocks.label: Connection pool and indexes
blocks.blurb: Few connections, cheap queries, stable pages.

blocks.label: Worker with dead letters
blocks.blurb: Delayed retries, a dead-letter queue, never blocked.

blocks.label: Authentication and tenancy
blocks.blurb: Verifies tokens and keys, scopes every query.

blocks.label: Lifecycle and canary
blocks.blurb: Readiness, drain, sticky canary and rollback.

01.hint: It sits between the service that pays for answers and the store every replica can read.

02.hint: It needs to know who is calling, so it comes right after the caller is identified, and its counters must be shared.

03.hint: It wraps every call that leaves for a model, and knows both models.

04.hint: The keys must survive restarts and be visible to every replica, next to the meals they protect.

05.hint: It wraps every request at the API and ships what it sees to the ops backend.

06.hint: The slow pages come from the guide's queries.

07.hint: Races happen where two writers touch the same row.

08.hint: It pulls jobs and calls the robots.

09.hint: First thing after the load balancer: nothing else may run for an unknown caller. Bot keys live in a table.

10.hint: The orchestrator asks it whether to send traffic, and it decides which release serves each caller.
